Generally looks like a pretty sound set of rules. Couple of thoughts (in no particular order)

1) "Submitting links to only one domain repeatedly" - given that the best submissions often come from the source (that is, not a vague blog post about a cnn article about a report of a study, but a link to the study itself), this rule seems like it could backfire a little. Imagine I'm a specialist in my field, and I want to post the best links possible about my field. For some fields/topic areas ("chemistry", "physics", etc) there are plenty of reasonable source options, but for someone that's specialized into something interesting, but very specific or esoteric ("life cycle of neutron stars", "genetic therapy advances in type-1 diabetes", etc), then there are likely only a few potential good sources.

I think the heart/spirit of this rule is right & proper, but perhaps a bit more leeway is in order. 9:1 may be too restrictive. It may be desirable to loosen that restriction, or at least consider some case-by-case scenarios.

2) "Self promotion is not allowed." (in posts, not comments) - i was unclear why this was crossed out. Can you clarify? It seems like the same commenting rules should probably apply (especially the clear-labeling, IMHO). If one wanted to take a more defensive stance to avoid blog-spam, perhaps allowing self-promoting posts but only for studies/reports/etc that you had a direct hand in.

3) "vaguely related to science, politically charged in nature, or containing bias" - As a few others have mentioned, this one worries me. What might be vague to one person is simply a high-level discussion to another. And, at least in the U.S., if you want to remove all politically charged posts, you may as well shut down some whole areas of science-posting. Again, though, I understand the spirit in which this rule was intended, and do like the intent. Perhaps - and I'm just spit-balling here - one way to get around the timezone/mod issue would be to use a "two man switch". If one mod thinks it could be a 'bad' article, it gets flagged, but only when a second mod agrees, does it get pulled. Or something along those lines.
